purpose: Make every TROQAR prototype variant and downstream BodyWar page preserve the image-derived dark athletic identity, Strava-first login posture, privacy copy, and logo system.

brand.name: TROQAR
brand.thesis: Running performance meets territory, people, and challenges.
languageNotes: Prefer short Portuguese action copy when the surface is product-facing.
Keep privacy and evidence caveats plain and visible.
Do not make the first screen feel like a generic SaaS dashboard.

logoSystem.markDescription: Hexagonal badge with orange upper/right stroke, green lower/left stroke, and a stylized runner whose orange upper body transitions into green stride/route motion.
logoSystem.wordmarkDescription: All-caps condensed athletic wordmark; TROQ is fire-orange and AR is territory-green.
logoSystem.taglineDescription: CORRA. CONECTE. CONQUISTE. with action words split orange, off-white, and green.
usageRules: Use the horizontal lockup in top bars when there is enough width.
Use the hex mark alone in compact mobile headers, bottom navigation, favicons, or app-icon contexts.
Do not recolor the mark into a single hue.
Do not place the logo on light card surfaces except for isolated export previews.

asphaltBlack.role: Full-page app background and logo negative space.

asphaltInk.role: Primary shell, top bar, and dark surface base.

panelRaised.role: Secondary panels and active dashboard cards.

fireOrange.role: Primary action, Strava connect, active challenge, running energy.

territoryGreen.role: Connected state, success, owned territory, verified-safe status.

coolGray.role: Secondary copy, labels, muted evidence notes.

deepBorder.role: Subtle borders that preserve dark-app depth.

display.role: TROQAR titles, route names, challenge titles, major metric numerals.

body.role: Forms, paragraphs, privacy copy, activity data, controls.

number.role: Distance, time, pace, stage counts, XP, ranking.

layoutRules: Design mobile-first and app-like; desktop may expand the same control surfaces, but must not become a landing page.
Use a dark full-viewport shell with compact dashboard panels, bottom navigation patterns, route cards, and athlete profile cards.
The first screen must show login/connection state, a clear Strava connect action, and a hint of profile/activity value.
Cards are allowed for repeated app objects; do not nest cards or float every page section as a card.
Use route/topographic line texture sparingly as background detail, not as a substitute for real route data.
Use stable dimensions for nav, controls, metric cards, and activity rows so content does not shift when auth state changes.
authAndPrivacyRules: Visible MVP login method is Strava only.
Provider extensibility may exist internally, but the first page must not show unrelated login providers.
Never render access tokens, refresh tokens, OAuth codes, expiry internals, or raw provider payloads.
Public Strava profile links are allowed only as display data with safe link text.
Activity summaries must stay redacted; route geometry and scoring claims are deferred until verified by backend evidence.

loginPage: Use the TROQAR lockup or mark in the first viewport.
Primary CTA is fire-orange and starts Strava auth.
Anonymous copy should say the app connects running, territory, and challenges without implying verified scoring yet.
topbar: Dark asphalt background, logo at left, account actions at right.
Actions must fit 390px mobile width without overlap.
Do not use pale toolbar chrome.
profileCard: Show safe athlete identity, public Strava link, connection state, and privacy promise.
Use green for connected state, gray for redacted/private data notes.
activityCard: Show distance, time, pace if present, sport type, eligibility, and preview evidence CTA.
Use orange for action and green only for safe/complete status.
routeOrTrackCard: Use territory/route context and controller metric.
Keep placeholder or preview status visibly distinct from verified state.

doNotUse: White admin dashboard visual language for the main app surface.
Beige, cream, sand, or tan dominant palettes.
Multiple visible login providers in the MVP first screen.
Decorative dark atmospherics that hide data, privacy caveats, or route status.
Verified, scored, or ranked evidence language before route geometry and evidence authority are implemented.
validationExpectations: JSON must parse before handoff export.
Future Studio variants should list this file in export-profile sourceRefs.
Future BodyWar Playwright checks should assert mobile no-overlap, Strava-only anonymous login, safe profile copy, and no token leakage.
Screenshots should visibly preserve dark asphalt shell, fire-orange CTA, territory-green success state, and TROQAR logo usage.
